\chapter{Complexity — Computable}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.Uncomputability.Computable
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module defines the machine-independent notion of a computable total string
function [AB09, \S 1.4, p.\ 20] --- some finite binary Turing machine computes it,
with no time constraint --- and proves the bridge back to the time-bounded notion:
any machine that computes a function without a stated time bound in fact computes
it within some time bound.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Existence of a time bound for a computing machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.Computes.exists_computesFunInTime}
\label{Turing.FinTM.Computes.exists_computesFunInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.Computes, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over
$\Sigma$, and let $f$ be a total function from strings over $\Sigma$ to strings
over $\Sigma$. If $M$ computes $f$ --- on every input $x$ it halts, after some
finite number of steps, with $f(x)$ on its output tape, with no stated time
bound --- then there exists a function $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that
$M$ computes $f$ within time $T$, i.e.\ on every input $x$ the machine $M$
halts with output $f(x)$ within $T(\abs{x})$ steps, where $\abs{x}$ is the
length of $x$. No monotonicity, positivity, or constructibility of $T$ is
claimed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Computable string function]
\lean{Complexity.Computable}
\label{Complexity.Computable}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.Computes}
A total function $f$ on bit strings (from $\{0,1\}^*$ to $\{0,1\}^*$) is
\emph{computable} if there exists a finite Turing machine over the binary
alphabet that computes $f$: on every input $x$ it halts, after some finite
number of steps, with $f(x)$ on its output tape. No time constraint is imposed
[AB09, \S 1.4, p.\ 20].
\end{definition}
